body.x: Korea Nuclear Power Robotics Co., Ltd. (KNR, CEO Sangbeom Nam) announced that it will participate in CES 2025, held from January 7th (Tuesday) to January 10th (Friday) in Las Vegas, USA, under the "K-Startup Pavilion."

Korea Nuclear Power Robotics provides advanced technologies and services required to maintain nuclear power plants, small modular reactors (SMRs), and atomic fusion power facilities. The ultra-compact EDM in-bore system supports maintenance in confined spaces. It enables the cutting and welding of coolant pipes in fusion breeding blankets from the interior without removing insulation.

In 2022, KNR completed a project to remove foreign objects from the interior of steam generators at the Kori Nuclear Power Plant, demonstrating the excellence of its EDM-based tube-cutting technology. The company has also developed boat sampling technology for welding areas on reactor heads and fire encapsulation technology that operates without power, setting new benchmarks in nuclear maintenance and safety.

KNR has established itself as an essential partner for safe and efficient nuclear facility operations. It collaborated with Doosan Enerbility on successful foreign object removal projects at nuclear plants, including the Shin Kori Unit 4 power plant.

Building on domestic achievements, KNR signed an MOU with EET, an equipment supplier for the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the UAE. It aims to supply solutions to Barakah and other global partners, addressing foreign object management challenges at nuclear plants worldwide.

Leveraging its domestic references, KNR is preparing to enter the U.S. market and was selected to participate in CES 2025 as part of its global strategy. Acknowledged for its next-generation nuclear technologies, KNR was named to the Ultra-Gap Startup 1000+ program and received the Minister of Trade, Industry, and Energy Award on the 14th Nuclear Safety and Promotion Day, solidifying its technical innovation and capabilities.

Through the SMR Industry Ecosystem Foundation Project, KNR is also dedicated to developing ultra-compact technologies for maintaining small modular reactors, enhancing maintenance efficiency, and creating a new industrial ecosystem.

body.x: KNR stated that its participation in CES aims to showcase innovative technologies applicable across industries beyond the nuclear sector and explore new market opportunities.

To address global industrial efficiency and safety challenges, KNR will highlight the versatility of its ultra-compact EDM technology, in-bore laser cutting and welding solutions for pipe interiors, and encapsulation-based fire suppression solutions.

CES serves as a global platform for technological innovation and industry advancements. KNR aims to showcase its capabilities to a worldwide market and seeks new industry partnerships and collaboration opportunities.

KNR’s ultra-compact EDM technology, applicable to SMRs, is an advanced electric discharge machining tool for precise and efficient cutting and processing within complex industrial systems. It maximizes precision and stability, proving effective even in high-difficulty environments. It also significantly reduces maintenance and manufacturing time and costs.

The in-bore laser cutting robot for pipe interiors uses ultra-compact laser technology to perform cutting and welding tasks within pipes. It simplifies maintenance processes by eliminating the need to remove insulation and adapts flexibly to various pipe structures.
KNR stated, “We plan to lead future industries, including SMR and fire safety solutions, while strengthening our position in emerging markets beyond the traditional nuclear maintenance sector.”
